disease: Herbal masala bolus for all Digestive Problems
symptoms: anorexia, indigestion, off feed, absence of rumination, impaction
ingredients: Kalimirch (black pepper) 10 gm, Jeera (cumin) 10gm, Dhaniya (coriander seeds) 20 gm, Fenugreek (methi) 20 gm, Ajwain (Trachyspermum ammi) 10 gm, Adrak (ginger) 50 gm, Haldi (turmeric) 50 gm (fresh), Gheekumari (Aloe vera) 100 gm, Galo / batindu (Tinospora cordifolia) stem and leaves 100 gm, Neem leaves 100 gm, Moringa / Sahjan (Moringa oleifera) leaves 100 gm, Guava leaves / Amrood (tender) 100 gm, Bari Chirmi / Chirputa (Cardiospermum halicacabum) 100 gm, Lahsun (garlic) 50 gm, Lallmirch (red pepper /chillies) 50 gm, Paan (betel leaves) 10 number, Tulsi leaves 50 gm, Tarwar leaves and flowers (Cassia auriculata) 100gm, Nariyal (Coconut) 100 gm, Gud (Jaggery) 100gm, rock salt 50 gm, Khaneka soda (Sodium bicarbonate) 100 gm
treatment: First grind all dry items in a mixi viz. black pepper, jeera, coriander seeds, fenugreek, ajwain, red chillies. Then grind all the fresh herbs viz. Aloe vera, curry leaf, garlic, tulsi, ginger, turmeric, coconut (grated), galo and tarwar. After that mix together both the above items. Now add jaggery (after making into small pieces), and rock salt, (sodium bicarbonate) and mix it thoroughly. At the end make a bolus of 100 gm each (lemon fruit size) and administer orally. For young animals (calf, sheep or goat) give half the quantity or reduce the quantity according to the body weight of animals. It can be given monthly once preferably in empty stomach. For problematic cases continue the treatment for 2-3 days.

symptoms: Lack of defecation, hard pelleted dung
ingredients: 100 gm neem leaves, Laxatives like castor oil, raw linseed oil (500ml), 100 gm of haldi (turmeric rhizome)
treatment:
1. Enema can be given (boil 10 litres of water after adding 100 gm neem leaves and cooled and administer through rectum of large animals). Avoid early stage pregnant animals.
2. Laxatives like castor oil, raw linseed oil (500ml) can be given for 1-2 days according to species and body weight of animal. Given as drench for 2-3 days or as required.
3. A decoction prepared with 100 gm of haldi (turmeric rhizome) in 1 litre of water may be given once daily for 1-3 days to large animals.

symptoms: Animals emaciated, thick body hairs, foul smelling stools with worms
ingredients: Leaves of nirgundi (Vitex negundo), Leaf petals of khorpad (Aloe vera), Neem seeds, Leaves of sangkupi (Clerodendrum inerme), Leaves of akamadar (Calotropis gigantea)
treatment: Neem, Nirgundi, Gheekumari, Sangkupi, Akamdar (Aak). They are to be taken at 1 kg each. All are to be ground well by sprinkling little water and filtered, obtaining 4 litres of herbal mixture. Then 30 ml of the extract is taken and administered for one adult sheep or goat. For younger sheep or goat less than 3 months old, 10 ml has to be administered orally. For adult cattle 100 ml has to be administered. This can be stored for more than one month. The dewormer arrests loose motion, results in solid dung free from obnoxious odor, increases grazing efficiency, and promotes health.

symptoms: Presence of parasites visible all over the body, animal emaciated, dull and death in severe cases
ingredients: Lahsun (Garlic), Tulsi, neem leaves, haldi (turmeric), seethapal seeds, Raimuniya (Lantana camara), Tobacco
treatment:
1. Lahsun (Garlic), Tulsi, neem leaves, haldi (turmeric), seethapal seeds each 10-20 gm are ground together and boiled in 250 ml of neem oil and applied over the surface of the body of large animal.
2. Whole plant of Raimuniya (Lantana camara) is chopped and crushed and diluted with the urine of cattle for 3 days and applied externally.
3. Boil tobacco leaves and stalk 250 gm in 2 lit. of water and add 5 lit. of water and spray over the body of 10-20 animals.

ingredients: Tulsi (Ocimum sanctum), Arusha (Adhatoda vasica), ginger, pepper, jaggery, Kantakari / kateli (Solanum surattense)
treatment:

symptoms: Shivering of the body and limbs, erect hairs, watery eyes, recumbent and unable to get up, off feed and water, reduction in the milk yield
ingredients: charcoal or wooden pieces, neem seeds 200 gm, Ajwain, haldi (jungli haldi), garlic, pepper 5 gm, rice or bajra
treatment:
1. Take a mud pot, put a few charcoal or wooden pieces, burn them for a few minutes and put off the fire. Add neem seeds 200 gm in the mud pot to produce smoke. Direct the smoke towards the head of the animal to inhale.
2. Ajwain, haldi (jungli haldi), garlic, pepper 5 gm each taken, ground together and diluted in hot water, administered orally twice a day.
3. Feed the animal with rice or bajra porridge by boiling in water with broken grains (500 gm).
4. Provide drinking water after boiling and cooling. Feed only dried hay or straw and avoid green fodder.

symptoms: Ulcers in mouth and cleft of hooves, drooping saliva and difficult to walk
ingredients: Haldi (Turmeric) 200 gm, coconut kernel extract (from 1 coconut), gheekumari (Aloe vera) 200 gm, palm jaggery 200 gm, common salt 100 gm, garlic 100 gm, pepper 50 gm, cumin 50 gm, fenugreek 50 gm, bananas, sesame oil
treatment:
1. Haldi (Turmeric) 200 gm (freshly harvested rhizome preferred), coconut kernel extract (from 1 coconut), gheekumari (Aloe vera) 200 gm, palm jaggery 200 gm, common salt 100 gm, garlic 100 gm, pepper 50 gm, cumin 50 gm, fenugreek 50 gm.
2. Ground turmeric, gheekumari, garlic, and grated coconut with sufficient water in a vessel. Powder pepper, cumin, fenugreek. Mix all ingredients thoroughly with water to make about 1 liter. Filter and administer orally.
Dose: 100 ml at a time for adult animals or 50 ml for young ones or sheep/goats. Before treatment, feed animals with 2 bananas soaked in 50 ml sesame oil (Til ka tel). Continue for 3 days.

treatment: Clean the mass with potassium permanganate solution (1 ml in 1 lit water) and sprinkle Epsom salt or sugar over it. Keep the animal in a slightly slanting position with head lower for at least a week.
